title: pipeline: introduce prefill/decode handshake with adaptive kernel handoff and KV-aware throttle
author: Asha Iyer
release_notes: Introduces a handshake between prefill and decode stages that enables an adaptive kernel handoff and KV-cache-aware throttling to reduce tail latency and microburst-induced KV thrashing. No API changes.
description:
Motivation: We observed two classes of production tail events for short (<=128 token)generation workloads: 1) microbursting where many concurrent prefill requests enter the runtime and cause KV-cache churn and eviction storms; 2) kernel cold-switch overhead where decode stage must switch kernel/code-paths mid-response for a small subset of requests, adding 10-30ms tail noise. This PR implements a lightweight handshake between prefill and decode so the scheduler can make an informed kernel handoff decision and apply KV-cache-aware backpressure.

What this change does (high level):
- Adds a prefill/decode handshake protocol (prefill_protocol.proto) where prefill includes a small header: model_hint, expected_decode_window (tokens), kv_version_hint, and preferred_kernel_mask. The handshake is intentionally small (few bytes) to keep cost negligible.
- Introduces HandshakeScheduler (runtime/scheduler/handshake_scheduler.py + C++ hotpath hooks) that maintains a short-lived per-request "handoff" state. The scheduler uses the handshake to:  a) choose an initial kernel candidate, b) reserve a kernel window slot (adaptive window) to avoid kernel cold starts during decode, c) apply KV-aware throttle tokens to stagger prefill admission when KV eviction pressure is high.
- Implements adaptive kernel handoff in kernel_selector.cpp: we added a moving-window heuristic that prefers kernels previously hot for similar model_hint+sequence_length buckets. This reduces per-request kernel initialization for mixed-model clusters.
- Adds KVThrottleManager (kv_throttle_manager.*) which tracks per-GPU KV eviction rate and issues short (10-200ms) prefill admission holds for low-priority requests. The throttle integrates with the existing priority queues so bursty traffic is smoothed without global capacity drops.
- Alignment/continuous-batching tweak: a light-weight microbatch aligner ensures decode-stage token window boundaries align with previously reserved kernel windows to let the handoff produce fewer kernel switches. This is a runtime-only optimization with a feature-flag and config knobs.

Benchmarks and numbers (internal perf lab):
- Workload: mix of 60% chat-short (max 64), 30% completion-short (max 128), 10% long tails (512), 8 concurrent clients at 100rps overall.
- Baseline (main): 95th latency for short responses = 128ms. With this PR: 95th latency = 105ms (18% reduction). P99 improved ~12%.
- KV eviction cycles reduced by ~26% under synthetic microburst tests. Throughput at steady-state unchanged (+1-2%).

Tests added:
- integration/test_prefill_handshake.py: end-to-end handshake + fallback when decode ignores handshake.
- bench_prefill_handoff.py: microbench harness comparing kernel switch counts with/without handoff.
- unit tests for kv_throttle_manager and kernel_selector heuristics.

Operational notes and rollout plan:
- Feature gated (runtime config: enable_prefill_handshake=false by default). We enable on internal "staging-prefill" cluster for 48h, then progressively enable for low-traffic tenants for one week, monitor handshake_events telemetry, kernel_switch_rate, and kv_eviction_rate.
- Added telemetry (metrics/telemetry/prefill_handshake_events.yaml) that emits: handshake_latency_ms, kernel_handoff_decision, kv_throttle_applied, throttle_duration_ms.
- Rollback: set enable_prefill_handshake=false and kv_throttle_disabled=true; scheduler state decays in-flight and does not block traffic.

Compatibility and fallback:
- The handshake is backward-compatible: decode stage treats missing handshake header as a neutral hint and falls back to current behavior. Throttle manager operates on a best-effort basis and will not drop requests.

Commits (summary):
- 92f3b49 Add prefill_protocol.proto and basic handshake plumbing
- d4a2c11 HandshakeScheduler initial implementation and python shim
- a7c9e03 Kernel selector: adaptive window and model_hint bucket mapping
- c1b6f2e KVThrottleManager with eviction detector and admission hold
- f6d0fff Tests and perf harness + docs

Files changed (high level): small but focused changes across serving runtime kernel selection, scheduler, KV manager and telemetry. No public API changes.

Why this is different from previous prefill/decode work: earlier PRs focused on speculative prefill chunking and stage overlap for throughput improvements. This PR is operating at the handshake level — providing an explicit, low-cost signal between stages to coordinate kernel selection and admission control. The goal is tail-latency smoothing and KV eviction reduction rather than raw throughput wins.

Documentation: docs/ops/prefill-handshake.md describes the feature, config knobs and troubleshooting steps. Example trace visualizer (tools/trace/handshake_visualizer.py) helps ops correlate handshake decisions with kernel switches.

TODOs and follow-ups:
- Expand model_hint taxonomy with automatic fingerprinting (ENG-7790).
- Investigate integrating handshake with regional routing to prefer co-located KV hot-shards.
- Evaluate handshake overhead at extremely high request fan-out (>1000 concurrent clients).
